participant_roles: Strategy=BasePermission; ConcreteStrategy=AllowAny, IsAuthenticated, IsEmployer, IsEmployee; Context=PermissionMixin (check_permissions, check_object_permissions, get_permissions); Client=CreateNewJob, UpdateJob
intent_and_evidence: Problem: each GraphQL mutation needs a different access rule. BasePermission declares has_permission/has_object_permission; four subclasses override has_permission (e.g. IsEmployer checks request.user.role == 'employer'). A mutation sets permission_classes (sub_mutations.py:30,54) and PermissionMixin.get_permissions instantiates them (graphql_mixins.py:49); check_permissions loops over them calling has_permission (23-24). All listed policies must pass, so it acts as a policy list. Application-defined, not framework.

participant_roles: AbstractClass=MutationMixin (not declared abstract); TemplateMethod=MutationMixin.mutate; Hook=resolve_mutation (not declared in the base class); ConcreteClass=CreateNewJob (hook from CreateNewJobMixin.resolve_mutation), UpdateJob (hook from UpdateJobMixin.resolve_mutation)
intent_and_evidence: Problem: every mutation must check permissions and handle denial the same way, while the work differs. mutate fixes the order: check_permissions(info, **input) then cls.resolve_mutation(...), and converts PermissionDeniedError into an error payload (63-68). The hook is supplied by the mixins listed first/after in the MRO (CreateNewJobMixin 306-318 saves a new Job; UpdateJobMixin 324-335 updates one). RelayMutationMixin (75-90) has the same shape but is not used in the inspected files, so it is not counted as a participant. Hook is implicit (no abstract method declared).
